paragraphs.source_en: With such progress, physicists have been motivated to see how much fur ther inflationary cosmology can go. Can it, for example, resolve the ultimate mystery, encapsulated in Leibniz's question of why there is a universe at all? Well, at least with our current level of understanding, that's asking for too much. Even if a cosmological theory were to make headway on this question, we could ask why that particular theory- its assumptions, ingredients, and equations -was relevant, thus merely push ing the question of origin one step further back. If logic alone somehow required the universe to exist and to be governed by a unique set of laws with unique ingredients, then perhaps we'd have a convincing story. But, to date, that's nothing but a pipe dream.
